sections.heading: What you're agreeing to
sections.body: You agree to a psychiatric evaluation and, if appropriate, treatment by a licensed psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner working with Legion Health. Visits happen by secure video. [Prototype placeholder text.]

sections.heading: What we'll explain
sections.body: Before any treatment, your provider will explain the benefits of the proposed treatment, other options, how treatment works, likely side effects, and what may happen without treatment. You can ask questions at any time.

sections.heading: Telehealth
sections.body: Video visits follow Texas rules for telehealth. A connection problem may interrupt a visit; your provider will call you back or reschedule. You should join from a private place.

sections.heading: Your choices
sections.body: You may stop treatment or withdraw this consent at any time by telling your care team. Stopping does not affect your right to future care.

sections.heading: Emergencies
sections.body: Legion Health is not an emergency service. If you are in danger, call 911. You can call or text 988 for the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.

sections.heading: What we retrieve
sections.body: You authorize Legion Health to request your prescription and medication history electronically from pharmacies, pharmacy benefit managers and health plans. [Prototype placeholder text.]

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Your care team uses this history to understand what you take or have taken, avoid harmful interactions and prevent duplicate or unsafe prescribing.

sections.heading: Read-only
sections.body: Retrieving your history does not change any of your prescriptions.

sections.heading: Sensitive information
sections.body: Some records, such as medications for substance-use treatment, carry extra legal protections. You give this authorization voluntarily.

sections.heading: How long
sections.body: This authorization lasts while you are a Legion Health patient. You may revoke it in writing at any time.

sections.heading: Our approach
sections.body: Legion Health does not prescribe controlled substances except when clinically necessary, as determined by your provider, and always within federal and Texas law. [Prototype placeholder text.]

sections.heading: Stimulants
sections.body: Medicines such as amphetamine salts and methylphenidate raise alertness and attention. Side effects can include reduced appetite, weight loss and sleep problems.

sections.heading: Checks before prescribing
sections.body: Before prescribing certain controlled substances, your provider checks the Texas Prescription Monitoring Program, as state law requires.

sections.heading: Your role
sections.body: You agree to use one pharmacy, take medicines only as prescribed, and tell your provider about every medicine you take.

sections.heading: Payment at time of service
sections.body: Your estimated cost for each visit is shown before you book. Your card on file is used for any copay, deductible or coinsurance. [Prototype placeholder text.]

sections.heading: Insurance
sections.body: Legion Health submits claims to your insurer. You remain responsible for non-covered services, deductibles, copays and coinsurance as determined by your plan.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: Tell us when your insurance changes. Claims denied because of outdated information may become your responsibility.

sections.heading: Missed visits
sections.body: Please cancel or reschedule at least 24 hours before your visit. [Fee policy placeholder: confirm with Legion.]
